nationalKeyInfo.title: Value-based procurement is the national standard
nationalKeyInfo.detail: The DHSC / NHS England / NHS Supply Chain national standard scores medtech tenders on wider value (social value, efficiency, patient & staff, supply chain, purpose) weighted ≥60%, with whole-life cost capped at 40%. Procurement must save money AND show value.
nationalKeyInfo.use: Frame every case as value, not price. Build it in the Value Case Calculator and hand procurement a figure they can take to finance.

nationalKeyInfo.title: New NHS Supply Chain online catalogue
nationalKeyInfo.detail: A new online catalogue and search rolled out from late 2025 (search by NPC, MPC, supplier, brand, GTIN or free text).
nationalKeyInfo.use: A genuine, non-salesy opener: “how are you finding the new catalogue?”

nationalKeyInfo.title: New Hospital Programme reset
nationalKeyInfo.detail: Reset in Jan 2025 into delivery Waves 0–3; costed ~£56bn (NAO, Jan 2026). RAAC-affected trusts are prioritised in Wave 1.
nationalKeyInfo.use: If your trust has a new build, get in at design stage — equipment is specified 12–24 months before it opens.

nationalKeyInfo.title: Carbon scored at tender (Evergreen)
nationalKeyInfo.detail: NHS Supply Chain requires Evergreen Level 1 (a Carbon Reduction Plan + net-zero commitment) at tender close from 6 April 2026.
nationalKeyInfo.use: Have your carbon and sustainability position ready — it is scored, not optional.

nationalKeyInfo.title: NIHR HealthTech Research Centres — the NHS route to your own evidence
nationalKeyInfo.detail: A network of NIHR-funded centres of excellence hosted inside NHS trusts across England, set up specifically to help medical device, diagnostic, IVD and digital companies develop, evaluate and validate health technologies. They support real-world evidence generation and health economics, so a supplier can build NHS evidence with an NHS partner rather than arriving with vendor data alone. Each centre has its own clinical focus.
nationalKeyInfo.use: The answer when a trust says 'show me it works here'. If your evidence is manufacturer-run or from another health system, this is a named, credible route to NHS-generated proof — and raising it marks you out as someone who understands how the NHS actually accepts new technology.

nationalKeyInfo.title: NHS Supply Chain has a clinical assurance gate, not just a commercial one
nationalKeyInfo.detail: The Clinical and Product Assurance function (CaPA) sits inside NHS Supply Chain. Registered clinicians — nurses, midwives and allied health professionals — work across its clinical, commercial, customer engagement and strategy directorates to make sure the medical devices, products and consumables it sources meet NHS standards of safety, quality and effectiveness. Clinical judgement sits inside the sourcing process itself, not only at the trust that eventually buys.
nationalKeyInfo.use: Stop treating a framework as a purely commercial decision. Clinical evidence, usability and patient-safety arguments carry weight inside NHS Supply Chain's own sourcing process, not just with your trust. Ask how the clinical assurance for your category was done and what it looked at.

trusts.name: Barking, Havering and Redbridge University Hospitals NHS Trust
trusts.context: Queen's Hospital in Romford and King George Hospital in Goodmayes, serving one of the fastest-growing populations in England. Financially this is a turnaround account: a reported deficit of £30.7m in 2024/25 sitting on an underlying deficit of £46m, with an adjusted financial performance deficit of £38.9m against £6.1m the year before. The recovery plan requires savings of £61m, equal to 6% of income. Leadership is unusually thin on permanence — Chief Executive, Chief Operating Officer and Chief People Officer are all interim as at 14/08/2026 — so expect decisions to take longer and large commitments to need more cover than usual.
trusts.news: The Board has a Finance, Investment and Performance Committee scrutinising delivery of the financial recovery plan and savings programme, chaired by Sue Lees. The trust's own recovery narrative names right-sizing medical staffing and slippage in medical premium savings as the problems to fix, and commits to “further efficiency programmes to maintain and ensure high function performance across all core theatre capacity”. Board papers for 2026/27 are published four days before each meeting but the trust's document library does not expose them directly, so the current-year financial position could not be verified here — the £61m figure is the plan set out in the 2024/25 annual report.
trusts.structure: Payment performance has deteriorated sharply and it matters if you are carrying stock: 83.1% of non-NHS invoices paid within target by volume in 2024/25, down from 91.5% the year before, and 87.4% by value against 96.2%. That is the largest single-year fall in payment performance of any trust profiled in the Hub, and it is consistent with a trust managing cash through a deficit. Spend over £30,000 is published monthly. The Finance, Investment and Performance Committee is the body scrutinising the savings programme, so proposals framed as recovery-plan contributions have a named audience. Not verified: the size and structure of the procurement team, the e-tendering portal used, and whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates — none is published on the trust's site.

trusts.name: East Suffolk and North Essex NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: Ipswich and Colchester hospitals plus community services across east Suffolk and north Essex. The 2024/25 accounts show a £38.6m deficit, but £43.8m of that is a non-cash asset impairment — on the control total NHS England actually judges them on, they delivered a £3.5m surplus against a £0.25m target. So this is not a trust in crisis; it is one that hit its number. The softer spot is the quality of its savings: £22.7m delivered but only £12.7m of it recurrent, and the auditors identified weaknesses in how cost improvement delivery is tracked. Both executive leadership posts a supplier cares about — Chief Executive and Chief Finance Officer — are held on an interim basis as at 14/08/2026, so major commitments may move slowly.
trusts.news: Two surgical hubs are the story for anyone selling into theatres: a dedicated elective orthopaedic centre with its own theatres, three wards and 72 inpatient beds, and a surgical hub at Ipswich opened July 2024 with three specialist theatres and a same-day admissions ward covering general surgery, ENT, oral surgery and urology. The Clacton Site Transformation and Redevelopment (STAR) will significantly increase diagnostics activity. Board papers for 2026/27 are published but the trust's document library does not expose the finance report directly — the current-year position is therefore not verified here.
trusts.structure: A trust that has put social value and local supply at the centre of how it buys, and says so in its own annual report: it is a member of the Suffolk and North East Essex ICB Procurement Anchor Group, states that it buys locally wherever possible from small and medium sized businesses, and in its soft facilities management tender required bidders to state how and to what extent they would achieve social value and sustainability objectives. If you have a Carbon Reduction Plan and a local supply or employment story, lead with it here — it is scored, not decorative. Contracts are published on the trust's own contract register and all spend over £25,000 is published monthly. Payment is reasonable: 77.8% of non-NHS invoices paid within target by volume and 89.8% by value in 2024/25. Not verified: the e-tendering portal used, and whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates.

trusts.name: Frimley Health NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: Frimley Park Hospital is RAAC-affected (over 65% of the estate) and the remedial works are actively reducing theatre and ward capacity. 2026–27 is a breakeven plan with NO deficit-support funding (they received £20.6m of it in 2025/26), carrying a £68.6m cost-improvement programme. The replacement hospital's preferred site (part of Pine Ridge Golf Club) was announced 16 June 2026; construction is not expected before 2028–29 and the trust has not confirmed a total cost (press reports c. £1.5–2bn).
trusts.news: Preferred new-hospital site announced 16/06/2026 (Pine Ridge); Sacyr UK provisionally selected via the Hospital 2.0 Alliance (Building Better Healthcare, 17/06/2026); a 'Procurement Programme Support' role is being recruited for the rebuild programme.
trusts.structure: Fully in-house procurement department handling c. £250m/year, in three teams — Systems & Catalogue, Supply Chain (inventory across all three hospitals), and Category Management & Purchasing (Archipelago offices near Frimley Park) — with directorate-aligned category leads and three procurement clinical nurse specialists. Rep visits must be booked via MIA (miaweb.co.uk). The new-hospital rebuild runs its own commercial/procurement function under the Commercial Director. The substantive Head of Procurement is not publicly named (post exists; predecessor left Nov 2023).

trusts.name: Guy's and St Thomas' NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: The largest clinical supplies buyer in this batch by a wide margin — £418m a year, more than Leeds, Nottingham and Birmingham put together — and the largest waiting list of any trust in the Hub directory. Financially it performs: a £12.7m surplus against a breakeven plan in 2024/25 on the measure NHS England judges it by. But it missed its savings target, delivering £72.1m of a £93.8m programme, and 2026/27 raises the bar to a £115m efficiency requirement under a trust-wide campaign called Future Ready. The single most important structural fact: procurement here is a shared service that also buys for four other trusts, so one relationship reaches well beyond Guy's and St Thomas'.
trusts.news: Reported to the Board on 22/07/2026: the breakeven plan for 2026/27 is underpinned by a £115m efficiency requirement, described as requiring “a sustained and disciplined response across all clinical groups and corporate directorates”, with the Future Ready campaign launched in April to drive it. The Board was told service pressures experienced in 2025/26 were likely to intensify. CQC service inspections began in mid-March. The procurement team's new operating model went live on 1 April 2025 and the next phase is a new operating model for the supply chain team, covering materials management, logistics and warehousing.
trusts.structure: Procurement at Guy's and St Thomas' is a shared service that also supports Lewisham and Greenwich NHS Trust, Great Ormond Street Hospital, South London and Maudsley, and Oxleas NHS Foundation Trusts — five trusts buying through one function. That changes the value of the account entirely: a product accepted here has a route into four other organisations without a fresh procurement relationship each time. The team completed an operating model review in the year to 2024/25 and the new structure and shared-service relationships went live on 1 April 2025, so the people and remits you dealt with before that date may have changed — confirm who owns your category now. The supply chain team (materials management, logistics, warehousing) is the next part to be restructured, so expect disruption and opportunity there. Clinically the trust is organised into clinical groups each with its own chief executive — Women's and Children's, Cancer Surgery, Integrated and Specialist Medicine, and Heart, Lung and Critical Care — which means the clinical buying conversation has a named group leader, not just a directorate manager. Not verified: the e-tendering portal used and whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates.

trusts.name: Hampshire and Isle of Wight Healthcare NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: A new organisation, not an old one with a new name: formed in 2024 from Southern Health, Solent NHS Trust and services from the Isle of Wight and Sussex Partnership, and 2025/26 is its first complete combined annual report. It is mental health, community and specialist services — not an acute trust — so the buying profile is completely different: clinical supplies are £23.1m here against £238m at Leeds. If you sell theatre consumables or implants this is the wrong door. If you sell into community nursing, mental health inpatient settings, prescribing or diagnostics, it is a single buyer covering a very large population. They delivered a £55.2m recovery programme in full last year, so they can execute — but the underlying deficit is still £22.0m.
trusts.news: 2025/26 closed with the full £55.2m savings requirement delivered, 63% of it recurrent, reducing the underlying deficit from £32.0m to £22.0m. The savings themes named for the year ahead are integration benefits — corporate right-sizing, estate optimisation and clinical service integration — alongside agency reduction and explicit improvements in procurement and prescribing. The trust has a plan to eradicate waits over 52 weeks across all adult community waiting lists within Q1 2026/27, and diagnostic activity has grown year on year, with extra support provided to University Hospital Southampton following a fire. MRI performance is named as significantly more challenged.
trusts.structure: The single most useful published fact for a supplier here: the trust reports including a requirement for a minimum 10% net zero and social value weighting in all relevant procurements. That is a tenth of the score decided before anyone looks at your product, so a Carbon Reduction Plan and a real social value offer are not optional extras in this account. Procurement and prescribing are both named as savings themes in their own right, which means efficiency proposals in those areas have a route to a receptive audience rather than having to displace something else on the agenda. Note the leadership position: Paula Anderson is Acting Chief Executive as at 14/08/2026, having been the substantive Chief Finance Officer and Deputy Chief Executive since October 2024, and no separate Chief Finance Officer is listed on the board page — so finance decisions may route through an acting chief executive with a finance brief. Not verified: the e-tendering portal used, the procurement team's size and structure, and whether a rep access system operates.

trusts.name: Leeds Teaching Hospitals NHS Trust
trusts.context: One of the largest acute teaching trusts in England, £2.12bn total operating income in 2024/25 across the LGI, St James's, Chapel Allerton, Wharfedale, Seacroft and the Leeds Children's Hospital. Eight consecutive years of surplus to 2024/25 — but 2026/27 is a breakeven plan carrying a £95m Waste Reduction Programme, and Q1 closed £14.0m in deficit, £3.1m adverse to plan, partly on under-delivery of that programme. The new hospital at the LGI sits in Wave 2 of the New Hospital Programme with no construction before 2033–2035, so the existing estate has to last: the trust describes itself as carrying one of the highest backlog maintenance levels in the NHS, much of it critical infrastructure. A trust that has been good at savings, is now being asked for more, and cannot build its way out.
trusts.news: Q1 2026/27 reported to the public Board on 30/07/2026: £14.0m year-to-date deficit against a breakeven plan, with a Fundamental Review risk range of breakeven (best), £49m deficit (mid) and £93.7m deficit (worst). Capital is running behind — £12.3m spent to 30/06/2026 against a £24.2m ask, with 40% of the programme due by September. New organisational strategy 2026–2029 published, built on People, Improvement & innovation, Partnerships and Outcomes.
trusts.structure: Procurement sits inside the Finance Directorate under the Chief Finance Officer, and is over 100 staff across five disciplines: Procurement and Contracting, Logistics and Materials Management, Supplier Relationship Management, Data and eProcurement, and Commercial Activity. Tendering runs through Atamis, the Health Family Single e-Commercial System — register once and the same account works across other health family organisations; opportunities also appear on Find a Tender and Contracts Finder, and the trust publishes a forward Commercial Pipeline worth reading before you approach. The team is accredited at 'Best' (91%) against the national Commercial Continuous Improvement Assessment Framework and holds Cabinet Office Customer Service Excellence accreditation, so expect a professional, process-led buyer rather than an informal one. Pathology is not bought trust-by-trust: the Pan Pathology Managed Service Contract is a collaborative contract spanning Leeds, Mid Yorkshire and Calderdale & Huddersfield. The trust does not publish a rep booking or accreditation system — Not verified whether one exists; ask your named contact.

trusts.name: Mid and South Essex NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: Broomfield, Basildon and Southend, the largest waiting list of any trust in the Hub directory, and the most financially distressed account in this batch. 2025/26 closed with an overall deficit of £112.9m even after £51.4m of national deficit support funding. More important for anyone selling here: the plan the trust has agreed with NHS England for 2026/27 reports a deficit of £78m, and the trust states in its own annual report that this does not meet national planning requirements and that it will need working capital support across the year. Capital is under tighter controls and prioritisation. Expect long approvals, heavy scrutiny of any new spend, and real interest only in things that release cash quickly.
trusts.news: Published 17/07/2026: the 2025/26 annual report records an NHS England adjusted financial performance deficit of £63.6m — £115.0m excluding deficit support funding — in line with the agreed forecast for the trust and the system. Board priorities named for the year are delivery of the financial recovery and efficiency programme with strengthened financial governance and oversight, and strategic oversight of capital with tighter controls and prioritisation. Most striking for a supplier: clinical supplies spend fell by £19.5m in the year, from £138.1m to £118.6m.
trusts.structure: Procurement and Contract Management runs on the Atamis database, so registration there is the practical route in and the same account carries across other health family organisations. The trust is organised as a group with a Group Chief Executive above hospital chief executives at Broomfield and Basildon, so a site-level conversation has a named owner while group-level decisions sit above them. Note how thin the permanent executive bench is: the Chief Financial Officer, Chief Nurse and the Executive Director for Strategic Elective Recovery and Transformation are all interim as at 14/08/2026. Combined with tighter capital controls and a deficit that NHS England has not accepted as compliant, this is an account where a large capital sale is unlikely to move quickly and a consumable or pathway saving is the realistic opening. Not verified: whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates.

trusts.name: Nottingham University Hospitals NHS Trust
trusts.context: One of the largest acute trusts in England — QMC, City Hospital and Ropewalk House — and financially the hardest-pressed trust in this batch. 2025/26 closed £12.2m in deficit against a breakeven plan, having delivered £67.6m of a £97.7m efficiency target. 2026/27 asks for £106m of savings and the Board has already been told the level of ambition must increase. The Board's own view is that the cost base is unsustainable relative to income, so this is not a trust looking for nice-to-haves: bring a cash-releasing number or expect a short meeting. Their estate cannot rescue them either — the Tomorrow's NUH rebuild is postponed to 2037 at the earliest and they carry the fourth largest maintenance backlog in the country.
trusts.news: Month 2 (May 2026) reported to the public Board on 09/07/2026: £23.0m year-to-date deficit, £6.1m adverse to plan, with a £4.5m year-to-date overspend on clinical supplies and services driven by higher-than-planned activity. Efficiency delivery £6.3m against a £7.1m year-to-date plan. A “Plan B” is being worked up for the parts of Tomorrow's NUH that cannot wait until 2037, with backlog maintenance named as a main priority. The National Rehabilitation Centre, a 70-bed purpose-built NHS facility near Loughborough and the first of its kind in the UK, is staffed and run by NUH and due to open.
trusts.structure: NUH operates a strict “no purchase order, no payment” policy — an invoice without an official PO number, and not on the exception list, is rejected outright. The PO is issued before you start supplying and is emailed to the address held in your supplier record, so get your supplier details right before anything ships. Invoices go to NHS Shared Business Services, not to the trust; accountspayable@nuh.nhs.uk handles disputes. They aim to pay within 30 days and frequently do not: in 2024/25 only 59.9% of non-NHS invoices were paid on time by volume and 58.4% by value, so price your working capital accordingly. Contracts over £25k are published on Contracts Finder. The distinctive route in for a device company is CHEATA — the Centre for Healthcare Equipment and Technology Adoption, a contract-based service embedded in the trust's Clinical Engineering department offering value propositions, health economic analysis, evidence gathering, NICE engagement and regulatory advice to manufacturers at any stage. Contacts Dr Sarah Bolton (Business Manager) and Sinead Barker (Programme Co-ordinator), nuhnt.cheata@nhs.net. Not verified whether NUH runs a separate rep booking or accreditation system for ward and theatre access.

trusts.name: Sheffield Teaching Hospitals NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: A £1.76bn teaching trust across the Royal Hallamshire, Northern General, Weston Park, Charles Clifford and Jessop Wing, and one of the few in this batch that is genuinely in surplus — £6.93m, 0.4% of turnover, on turnover up 11.5%. That makes it a different sell from the turnaround trusts: they are not desperate, so a pure price argument carries less weight, and the trust says plainly that 2025/26 brings “an even more constrained financial position”. Their stated approach is driving out unnecessary variation rather than blanket cuts, which favours suppliers who can evidence standardisation and reduced variation over those offering a discount.
trusts.news: Clinical supplies spend rose more than a fifth in a year, to £164.3m. The trust has almost eliminated the longest waits for treatment while its waiting list grew 0.7%. Its stated priorities for the year are “driving out unnecessary variation, refining our ways of working and through partnerships explore how we deliver the best value for the resources we are given”, navigated as a partner in the wider South Yorkshire system rather than alone.
trusts.structure: Two published procurement commitments are directly actionable for a supplier. First, social value is a part of all competitive procurements and environmental considerations are built into procurement processes — so it is scored, not decorative. Second, and more unusually, the procurement teams are explicitly working to increase the use of local businesses and suppliers specifically to reduce the road miles in their supply chain and support the local economy. If you have a Yorkshire or northern distribution point, warehouse or manufacturing site, that is a scoring argument here and not merely a nice story — quantify the road miles saved. Note the trust runs two Chief Medical Officers, split into Development and Operations, so the right clinical sponsor depends on whether you are proposing a new service or improving an existing one. Not verified: the e-tendering portal used, the procurement team's size, and whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates.

trusts.name: Somerset NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: An unusually integrated trust — acute (Musgrove Park and Yeovil District), community and mental health services under one board — which means a product with a pathway story spanning hospital and community has a single buyer here rather than three. The 2024/25 accounts show a £28.6m deficit, and 2026/27 carries a cost improvement plan of £80m, around 6.6% of operating expenses. They are delivering: May 2026 was breakeven to plan with CIP £0.4m ahead. The Board's stated worry is not the total but the mix — the pace of transformational savings and continued reliance on agency staffing. Something that structurally removes cost, rather than shaving a price, is what they are short of.
trusts.news: Reported to the public Board on 14/07/2026: May 2026 deficit of £3.347m, breakeven to plan; £2.680m of CIP delivered in the month, £0.404m above plan, and £5.081m cumulatively, £0.528m favourable year-to-date. The Board recorded concerns about “the pace of transformational savings, continued reliance on agency staffing” given the scale of savings required during 2026/27. The 2025/26 capital programme was delivered close to plan with a small underspend and the trust ended the year with a strong cash position.
trusts.structure: £80m of savings for 2026/27, of which £27.3m is business-as-usual CIP pushed down to clinical and non-clinical services to offset pay and non-pay inflation — that portion is devolved to budget holders, so a departmental conversation can carry real weight here rather than having to start at the centre. The remainder is transformational, which is where the Board says delivery is slowest and where a supplier with a genuine pathway change has the best hearing. Their integrated structure means acute, community and mental health procurement sit under one executive team. Not verified: the e-tendering portal used, the size and structure of the procurement team, and whether a rep booking or accreditation system operates — none is published on the trust's website.

trusts.name: University Hospitals Birmingham NHS Foundation Trust
trusts.context: Four hospitals — Queen Elizabeth Birmingham, Heartlands, Good Hope and Solihull — and one of the largest trusts in England. Financially it is under formal NHS England scrutiny: the trust reported an overall deficit of £69.5m in 2024/25 and, on the adjusted measure NHS England judges it on, a £0.9m surplus reached only after a Financial Recovery Plan agreed in September 2024 in response to an £81.4m adjusted deficit at month eight. It is rated 4 — Investigation and Intervention — under the NHSE Rapid Intervention process. The savings that got them there do not repeat: over half were non-recurrent, so the same gap reopens each year. A trust that needs recurrent, provable savings, not one-offs.
trusts.news: The 2024/25 accounts record control weaknesses that delayed the draft accounts and the audit, causing the trust to miss the national timetable. Clinical supplies spend rose to £251.3m. No 2026/27 board papers were publicly locatable on the trust's website as at 14/08/2026 — unlike Leeds and Nottingham, UHB does not publish an accessible board pack archive, so the current-year position here is not verified. Ask your contact directly rather than assuming the 2024/25 picture still holds.
trusts.structure: Unusually, each of the four hospitals has its own Hospital Executive Director sitting outside the main Board — Matt Metcalfe (Queen Elizabeth), Dr Rifat Rashid (Heartlands), Simon Jarvis (Good Hope) and Martin Richardson (Solihull). That matters for targeting: a site-level conversation has a named owner, and a trust-wide pitch has four internal customers, not one. Efficiency is benchmarked through the national Reference Cost Index, GIRFT and Model Hospital data, and the trust says this is shared with the hospital sites for planning — so GIRFT and Model Hospital comparators are the language that lands here. Payment performance is mid-range: 76.9% of non-NHS invoices paid within target by volume, 73.4% by value in 2024/25. Not verified whether UHB runs a rep booking or accreditation system, or which e-tendering portal it uses.
